mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month coincides with a decline in 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain statistically indistinguishable from a pre-tightening period (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in CPIAUCSL (inflation) for three consecutive months are associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate lower future rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes where FEDFUNDS remains above 5%, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a neutral benchmark (mean of prior 20-day returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) accompanied by a simultaneous drop in UNRATE (unemployment) predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as wage growth pressures weigh on equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.5 percentage points
regime_hint: labor market tightening before a recession
failure_condition: Over 12 months, 60-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained labor market tightening (p-value for regime shift < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in GDPC1 (real private demand) exceeding 4% of the prior quarter's level coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong demand signals robust economic growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by more than 4% from prior quarter in a month
failure_condition: In contractionary supply regimes (INDPRO < 90), the signal fails to predict positive returns (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both INDPRO (industrial production) and HOUST (housing starts) for two consecutive months predict negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as weak manufacturing and construction activity suggest economic softening.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months AND HOUST falls for two consecutive months
regime_hint: early signs of soft landing turning into softness
failure_condition: Over 30 days, the 5-day forward returns remain positive despite repeated double-month declines in both proxies (IC < 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE above 4% in a month while PAYEMS remains flat is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as rising unemployment weakens consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.5pp in a month and PAYEMS does not increase
regime_hint: labor market cooling after a boom
failure_condition: In regimes where GDP growth is positive (>2%), the signal fails to predict negative returns (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months in a non-stagflation regime is followed by a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as markets price in lower future policy rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls for three consecutive months and inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3% for the same period
failure_condition: Over 90 days, 60-day forward returns do not outperform a neutral benchmark (mean of prior 60-day returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 8% from the prior month in conjunction with a rising HOUST (housing starts) by 5% signals resilient consumer and housing demand, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >8% from prior month AND HOUST increases by >5% from prior month
regime_hint: resilient demand cycle in a post-pandemic environment
failure_condition: In recessions (PAYEMS < 90% of peak), the interaction fails to predict positive returns (IC < 0.05).
